plan.strategy: Establish the measured baseline with the unmodified seed: specialized fast launcher calling the compiled FlagTree launcher directly for the steady-state contiguous path, ordinary Triton launch for cold/misaligned cases, strided kernel for non-contiguous inputs.
plan.code_changes: None; seed written verbatim to tmp/main.py.
plan.hypothesis: Baseline measurement of the seed across the full 24 correctness and 12 timing workloads, to identify which timing workloads limit geo_mean speedup.

expected_effect.mechanism: No change; records the reference point for later experiments.

conclusion.root_cause: Baseline established with the seed. All 36 workloads pass; geo_mean 0.629 with the worst workload log10_-timing-3 at 0.471. Two independent limiters are visible: (a) every shape up to 1M elements sits at a flat ~17.4us per call, i.e. host-dispatch bound rather than device bound, while torch.log10_ dispatches in 10.0-12.3us; (b) the three 4096x4096 shapes are device bound at 33.9/38.1/38.9us versus 16.0/25.3/26.0us, i.e. the Triton elementwise kernel is 1.5-2.1x slower on device.
conclusion.next_suggestion: Reduce the steady-state host path: key the specialization cache by the exact device pointer (which also removes a latent stale-pointer hazard in the seed, where a different tensor with the same numel and 16-byte alignment reused the first pointer), keep the prebuilt pointer wrapper object instead of rebuilding it, and cut the per-call Python to one data_ptr, one numel, one dict lookup, one dtype check, one contiguity check, one current-stream read and the compiled launch.
conclusion.strategy_evolution: Seed measured first so that later host-path and device-path changes have an authoritative reference point.

plan.strategy: Shrink the steady-state host path to the compiled-launcher floor by caching each specialization on the exact device pointer and prebuilding its pointer wrapper object.
plan.code_changes: run() now keys the specialization cache by the exact (numel, device pointer) pair instead of (numel, pointer&15), and _make_launch builds the pointer wrapper object once per specialization so the steady-state path performs only data_ptr, numel, one dict lookup, one dtype identity check, one is_contiguous check, one current-stream read and the compiled launch. Kernels unchanged; the device path is identical to the baseline so any delta is attributable to host dispatch.
plan.hypothesis: Every measured shape with numel <= 1M is host-dispatch bound (flat ~17.4us regardless of size), so trimming per-call Python overhead while keeping the same device kernel raises those nine workloads' speedups without affecting the three 4096x4096 workloads.

expected_effect.mechanism: Removing the remaining redundant Python work per call lowers host dispatch from ~12.1us toward the ~8-9us compiled-launcher floor, which raises the nine host-bound timing workloads (1K-1M elements) whose measured per-call time is currently ~17.4us versus torch's 10.0-12.3us.

profile.summary: mixed: The 4096x4096 2-byte cases are vector-pipeline dominated, and their per-element vector cost is 1.4-1.7x the float32 path, float32 4096x4096 is MTE-busy but the vendor reports both DMA directions below 80% bandwidth utilization when active, Summed marginal pipeline activity approximately equals kernel duration on all five profiled shapes, consistent with little load/compute/store overlap

conclusion.root_cause: Steady-state host dispatch was dominated by avoidable Python work plus a wrapper object rebuilt per specialization; with it removed the nine host-bound shapes are within 1.4-2.4us of torch.log10_ and the residual gap to 1.0 is the ~8us compiled-launcher floor plus ~2us of device time.
conclusion.perf_gap_analysis: Frozen expectation was an increase in geo_mean from the nine host-bound workloads with no change on the three 4096x4096 ones. Observed: geo_mean 0.6292 -> 0.8026 (+27.6%). The nine shapes up to 1M elements dropped from 16.7-17.5us to 12.0-13.1us (speedups 0.84-0.95, e.g. log10_-timing-9 0.615 -> 0.954, log10_-timing-10 0.586 -> 0.899), which is the predicted host-dispatch reduction. The three 4096x4096 shapes were unchanged within noise (33.89/38.12/38.97us versus 33.88/38.12/38.92us), exactly as planned, and they are now the bottleneck, with log10_-timing-3 at 0.468. All 36 workloads still pass, including the 24 correctness cases, so the exact-pointer cache key preserved semantics.
conclusion.next_suggestion: Attack the three 4096x4096 shapes, which are now the whole remaining gap (0.468/0.664/0.671 versus 0.84-0.95 for every host-bound shape). Direct-launcher device measurements show the one-tile-per-program kernel costs 21.1us for a pure copy and 34.1us with the log, so the math is serialized after the DMA; unrolling 2 or 4 tiles per program already reaches 30.5us (fp16), 31.3us (fp32) and 35.0us (bf16). Test whether a chunked loop carrying two explicit tiles per iteration reaches the 40-program copy floor of 17.5us.
conclusion.debug_lesson: Paired target probes showed the seed's specialization cache was keyed on (numel, pointer&15) while the pointer wrapper object was built once, so a second tensor with the same extent and alignment would have reused a stale address; keying on the exact pointer both removes that hazard and lets the wrapper be prebuilt.
conclusion.strategy_evolution: Baseline isolated two limiters (flat ~17.4us for numel<=1M, and 1.5-2.1x slower device time at 4096x4096). The host limiter is now fixed; the device limiter on the three large shapes is next.

plan.strategy: Use unrolled multi-tile per-program kernels for large exactly divisible shapes so DMA bursts and log math from different tiles can overlap.
plan.code_changes: Added _log10_x4 (4 tiles of BLOCK per contiguous program) and _log10_x2 (2 tiles of BLOCK) plus a dtype-aware selection in _make_launch: for numel >= 4194304 and numel % 32768 == 0 and element size <= 4, 16-bit dtypes use _log10_x4 with BLOCK=8192 and 32-bit dtypes use _log10_x2 with BLOCK=16384, both with grid = numel/32768 and no tail mask. Every other shape keeps the previous single-tile path, so the nine host-bound shapes are untouched.
plan.hypothesis: The three 4096x4096 workloads are limited by serialized DMA-then-math inside each program: a pure copy costs 21.1us but the log kernel costs 34.1us, so math adds 13us instead of overlapping. Splitting a program's 32768 elements into 2-4 tiles whose loads all issue before the math lowers those shapes to about 30.5us (fp16), 34.9us (bf16) and 31.3us (fp32), as measured through directly bound compiled launchers.

expected_effect.mechanism: Issuing all loads of a program before any math lets the second, third and fourth DMA bursts overlap the log computation of earlier tiles, and keeping the same 32768 elements per program retains the measured best scheduling granularity.

conclusion.root_cause: Per-program unrolled tiles do let the second load issue before the first log, cutting fp16 4096x4096 from 33.9us to 30.25us and bf16 from 38.1us to 34.7us, but the 32-bit two-tile form (BLOCK=16384) is 1.23-1.43x slower than the single 32768-element tile in the formal measurement, so the change was net negative as submitted.
conclusion.perf_gap_analysis: Frozen expectation: all three 4096x4096 shapes improve (predicted 30.5/34.9/31.3us on probe evidence) with the nine host-bound shapes untouched. Observed on the original measurement: fp16 33.89 -> 30.25us and bf16 38.12 -> 34.73us, matching the probe, but fp32 38.97 -> 55.87us and the host-bound shapes rose from 12.0-13.1us to 15.6-18.1us although their code path did not change. The whole-suite retest reproduced the device numbers for fp16 (30.249 vs 30.252us, ratio 0.9999) and bf16 (34.730 vs 34.729us, ratio 1.0000) and pulled the host-bound shapes back to 10.65-11.87us, confirming the host shift was environmental, but fp32 stayed bad at 48.11us (0.530 versus the 0.671 of the single-tile form). So the mechanism is confirmed for 16-bit and refuted for 32-bit: geo_mean 0.8026 (round 2) -> 0.6855 original / 0.7636 retest, i.e. no net gain while fp32 is included.
conclusion.next_suggestion: Restrict the unrolled multi-tile path to 16-bit element types only: keep _log10_x4 with BLOCK=8192 for numel >= 4194304 and numel % 32768 == 0 on fp16/bf16, and leave 32-bit shapes on the single 32768-element tile, which is 39.0us versus 48.1-55.9us for the two-tile form. That keeps the two reproducible device wins and removes the fp32 regression.
conclusion.debug_lesson: Whole-suite remeasurement separated environment drift from candidate effect: the host-bound workloads moved 12.0->16.5us and back to 10.7-11.9us with byte-identical host code, while the device-bound 4096x4096 numbers reproduced to four digits, so only the device numbers were usable for judging this change.
conclusion.strategy_evolution: Round 2 fixed the host limiter; round 3 established that the remaining device limiter is only partly addressable by tile unrolling, and only for 16-bit element types.
